part.text:
I added Handlebars-based template engine support to the static site generator:

**New module** `src/templateEngine.ts` — a `TemplateEngine` class wrapping Handlebars: compiles per-directory templates/layouts, auto-registers all `.hbs` files in `partials/` as includes, caches compiled templates, and throws clear errors for missing templates/layouts.

**Directory structure** (checked into the repo):
- `templates/page.hbs`, `templates/post.hbs`, `templates/index.hbs` — page/index body templates
- `templates/layouts/default.hbs` — layout with `{{{body}}}` placeholder, includes header/nav/footer partials
- `templates/partials/header.hbs`, `nav.hbs`, `footer.hbs` — reusable includes

**Frontmatter support**: `PageFrontmatter` gained optional `template` and `layout` fields (parsed in `markdown.ts`), defaulting to `'page'`/`'default'` when unset. `content/hello-world.md` now demonstrates `template: post`.

**Wiring**: `templates.ts` now delegates to `TemplateEngine`, pre-escaping all values in TS (existing `escapeHtml`) so Handlebars stays purely structural. `build.ts` gained a `templatesDir` option (default `./templates`), and `cli.ts` gained a matching `--templates` flag — added without breaking the existing `parseArgs` exact-equality tests.

Verified with a real `bin/ssg.js build` run that layouts, partials, and per-page template overrides render correctly in actual output HTML.
